title: Python Control Flow, Strings and Encoding: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision notes on Python branching, loops, match, comprehensions, operators and truthiness, then f-strings, str methods and the Unicode vs bytes split. Ends with a one-page cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Branching, Loops and Match
points: if/elif/else runs the first true branch only; the conditional expression is `a if cond else b`
for iterates any iterable; `range(start, stop, step)` excludes stop; `enumerate(xs, start=1)` and `zip(a, b)` replace index juggling
`for`/`while` `else` runs only if the loop ended without `break`; it is skipped on break, and runs on zero iterations
`match` does structural pattern matching: literals, `case [x, y]`, `case {'k': v}`, `case Point(x=0)`, `case A | B`, guard `case n if n > 0`, and `_` as the wildcard
A bare name in `case` captures rather than compares; use a dotted name such as `Color.RED` to compare against a constant

chapters.title: Comprehensions and Generators
points: List `[f(x) for x in xs if cond]`; dict `{k: v for ...}`; set `{x for ...}`; filter goes at the end, a conditional expression goes before `for`
Nested loops read left to right in the same order as the equivalent for statements: `[x for row in m for x in row]`
Generator expression `(x for x in xs)` is lazy and single-use; `sum(x*x for x in xs)` needs no extra brackets
The comprehension variable is local to the comprehension and does not leak, unlike a for-loop variable
Use a plain loop when the body has side effects or needs more than two clauses; a comprehension is for building a value

chapters.title: Operators and Truthiness
points: Falsy values: `None`, `False`, `0`, `0.0`, `''`, `[]`, `{}`, `()`, `set()`, `range(0)`; everything else is truthy, and custom classes use `__bool__` then `__len__`
`and`/`or` return an operand, not a bool: `x or 'default'` returns the first truthy value and `a and b` returns the first falsy value, both short-circuiting
`==` compares value and `is` compares identity; use `is None`, never `is 0` or `is 'a'`
Chained comparisons `1 < x <= 10` evaluate x once; `//` floors toward negative infinity (`-7 // 2 == -4`) and `%` takes the divisor's sign
Walrus `if (n := len(xs)) > 3:` assigns inside an expression; `in` tests membership and is O(1) for set/dict but O(n) for list

chapters.title: f-strings and str Methods
points: f-string format spec is `{value:[[fill]align][sign][0][width][,][.precision][type]}`, for example `{x:>8.2f}`, `{n:,}`, `{n:08b}`, `{p:.1%}`, `{n:#x}`
`{x!r}` calls repr; `{x=}` prints `x=value` for debugging; nested fields work, as in `{x:{w}.{p}}`
Split and join: `s.split()` with no argument splits on any whitespace and drops empties, `s.split(',', 1)` limits the splits, `', '.join(items)` needs all str items
Strip and test: `strip/lstrip/rstrip(chars)` treat chars as a set; `removeprefix/removesuffix` remove an exact string; `startswith(('a','b'))` accepts a tuple
Strings are immutable: `replace`, `upper` and the rest return new strings, `s.find` returns -1 where `s.index` raises, and building in a loop with `+=` is slow, so use `join`

chapters.title: Unicode, Bytes and Encoding
points: `str` is a sequence of Unicode code points and `bytes` is raw 8-bit values; `s.encode('utf-8')` gives bytes and `b.decode('utf-8')` gives str, so they never mix: `'a' + b'a'` raises TypeError
UTF-8 is variable length (1 to 4 bytes) and ASCII-compatible, so `len('é')` is 1 while `len('é'.encode())` is 2
Always pass `encoding='utf-8'` to `open()` and `.encode()`/`.decode()` because the default depends on the platform; read binary files with mode `'rb'`
`errors='replace'` or `'ignore'` hides bad data and `'strict'` (the default) raises UnicodeDecodeError/UnicodeEncodeError; `'backslashreplace'` helps debugging
`ord('A')` is 65 and `chr(65)` is 'A'; the same visible text can differ in code points, so normalize with `unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)` before comparing

chapters.title: Python Control Flow and Strings Cheat Sheet
points: Control flow: `if/elif/else`, `a if c else b`, loop `else` runs only when there was no `break`, `match/case` with `_` wildcard and guards
Comprehensions: `[e for x in xs if c]`, `{k: v ...}`, `{e ...}`, `(e ...)` lazy; the loop variable stays local
Truthiness and operators: empty and zero are falsy, `or`/`and` return operands, `is None`, `//` floors, `1 < x < 5` chains
Formatting: `{x:>8.2f}` `{n:,}` `{n:08b}` `{p:.1%}` `{x!r}` `{x=}`; `split()`, `join`, `strip`, `removeprefix`, `replace` returns new
Encoding: `str` is text and `bytes` is data; `.encode('utf-8')` and `.decode('utf-8')`, always set `encoding=`, normalize NFC before compare
